purpose: Smelling salts are used to help revive someone who has fainted or feels like they might faint. They can also be used to briefly boost alertness. They work very quickly and are meant for short-term, occasional use only.
how_it_works: When you hold the smelling salts under your nose, the strong ammonia fumes irritate the lining of your nose and lungs. This sends a quick signal to your brain to breathe faster and deeper. That sudden rush of oxygen helps bring you back to alertness or consciousness within seconds.
common_side_effects: The most common effects include a strong burning or stinging sensation in the nose and throat, watery eyes, and a brief feeling of discomfort in the airway. These feelings go away very quickly after you move the salts away from your nose.
warnings: Do not hold smelling salts directly under your nose for more than a second or two — too much exposure can be harmful to your airways. Never use them on someone who has a head or neck injury without medical guidance. Keep out of reach of children. Do not swallow. If someone does not wake up after using smelling salts, call 911 immediately because they may need emergency medical care.
typical_dosing: Hold the broken capsule or open bottle about 4 to 6 inches below the nose and allow the person to briefly inhale the fumes for just 1 to 3 seconds. One brief whiff is usually all that is needed. Do not use repeatedly without medical advice.
